headline: Semiconductors Lead Broad Retreat as Geopolitical Crosscurrents Grip Monday's Session
body_html:
Equities are broadly lower at midday Monday, with declining issues outpacing advancers by nearly two to one across the 549-name universe — 352 names in the red versus 197 in the green. The dominant theme is risk aversion: mounting tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, an escalating North American trade dispute, and a pivotal macroeconomic week centered on Jackson Hole and a key U.S. inflation reading are collectively keeping buyers on the sideline.

Semiconductors are the session's clear laggard, off more than three percent as a group, with memory and equipment names absorbing the heaviest selling. Sandisk has shed nearly seven percent while FormFactor has fallen more than six. Energy shares are also under meaningful pressure, down roughly 1.8 percent, even as crude-supply anxieties swirl around Hormuz — a paradox traders attribute to demand-destruction fears and a strengthening gold bid drawing capital toward safe havens instead. Consumer and homebuilder stocks are the only sectors trading in positive territory, up 0.7 and 0.56 percent respectively.

The standout mover of the session is Napco Security Technologies, surging more than eleven percent on volume. Into the close, watch the semiconductor complex and the dollar, which is hovering near multi-month lows, for direction signals as the geopolitical news cycle remains fluid.

briefs.headline: Iran's Hormuz Threat Rattles Energy Markets but Fails to Lift Oil Names
briefs.body: Tehran's warning of fines and confiscation for as many as 45 tankers navigating the Strait of Hormuz has injected fresh uncertainty into crude supply chains. Despite the headline risk, energy equities are among Monday's worst performers, down roughly 1.8 percent, as traders appear more focused on demand concerns and the prospect of broadened U.S. secondary sanctions on Iranian oil flows.

briefs.headline: Trump Lifts Canada Auto Tariff Threat to 50%, Deepening Trade-War Fears
briefs.body: The White House signaled it would raise tariffs on Canadian automobile imports to 50 percent, a sharp escalation in the ongoing bilateral trade dispute. The announcement is weighing on industrials and materials sentiment mid-session, with both sectors trading in negative territory and investors reassessing cross-border supply-chain exposure heading into the second half of the year.

briefs.headline: Gold Bid Strengthens Ahead of Inflation Data and Jackson Hole
briefs.body: Precious metals are extending a rally as investors seek cover before a closely watched U.S. inflation print and the Federal Reserve's annual Jackson Hole gathering. The dollar's slide to near multi-month lows is amplifying gold's appeal, drawing capital that might otherwise support risk assets and contributing to the cautious tone across equity markets Monday.

briefs.headline: Napco Security Surges More Than Eleven Percent to Top the Leaderboard
briefs.body: Napco Security Technologies is the session's decisive standout, jumping 11.37 percent and commanding attention across the tech-security space. The move stands in sharp contrast to the broader market's defensive posture and has analysts watching whether the name can hold its gains into the final hour as overall sentiment remains fragile.

briefs.headline: Vital Farms and Celsius Holdings Anchor a Resilient Consumer Tape
briefs.body: Premium-food producer Vital Farms is up 7.85 percent and energy-drink marketer Celsius Holdings has gained 3.82 percent, helping the Consumer sector post the day's best performance at plus 0.7 percent. The relative strength suggests investors are rotating toward domestically oriented, brand-driven consumer names as macro uncertainty discourages exposure to more cyclical segments.

briefs.headline: UPS Commits $2 Billion to International and Healthcare Logistics Build-Out
briefs.body: United Parcel Service announced a $2 billion investment directed at expanding its international operations, healthcare logistics, and supply-chain capabilities. The commitment underscores sustained institutional demand for specialized logistics infrastructure even as broader industrial stocks face selling pressure Monday, with the industrials sector off about 0.81 percent mid-session.
